scope: TRAIN-only pole-time diagnostic; no model training, warning recalibration or reserved-design evaluation
noise_reference: Fixed initial ordinary-response sensor RMS within each design; paired Gaussian draw seed20261012+design_integer+replicate, independent channels. Never percent of shrinking instantaneous response.
window_contract: N samples span (N-1)*dt; ratio(t)=end_ratio-rate*(end_time-t). Fixed and ramping controls share end ratio, ordinary initial state, zero input, noise draw and absolute noise floor. Critical-only initialization uses the physical critical eigenvector at the starting ratio, matched initial sensor RMS; diagnostic positive control only.
estimator: Existing LS-ESPRIT, lag64, up to8 mode pairs, same leading51 measured calibration samples, cap50 before estimation. Record saturation and usable fraction; retain failed identification.
report: Select one estimated pole nearest end-reference frequency; compare that SAME pole to start/midpoint/end references. Report signed alpha and relative frequency errors, near-frequency retention, reference-frequency continuity, paired ramp-minus-fixed alpha estimates and availability. No model point estimate is changed.
hypotheses: Residual128ms ramp bias: clean critical-only estimates differ from matched-end stationary estimates and fit earlier-time references better
Mode-mixture error: stationary ordinary estimates fail where stationary critical-only controls recover
Noise-limited identification: clean recovery degrades at the fixed1% noise floor, independently of ramp rate
limitations: Four previously inspected original TRAIN designs and one paired noise draw; not blind confirmation
Critical-only excitation and reference poles are simulator diagnostics, never deployed predictor inputs
128ms is sample count; actual first-to-last span is127ms
Synthetic noise and ratio-rate settings are sensitivity controls, not deployment specifications
